alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.why_not_default: Grafana only displays data that the Collector, Loki and Prometheus already keep; it does not collect or store telemetry. In observability/receipt.json (line 292), the agent-browser screenshot predates the SDK receipt panel. observability/backends/receipt.json says 'No dashboard UI acceptance in this receipt' (line 103), and the restart check is 'not separate proof of unique SQLite-only user state' (line 156). The tag and packaged build commits also differ (`grafana_tag_build_commit_equal` false). It works as a view, not as the retention layer.

alternatives.name: alertmanager
alternatives.why_not_default: Alertmanager only routes alerts from Prometheus. `amtool check-config` exited 0. On the local loopback fixture it sent 1 firing and 1 resolved notification, but `external_delivery_tested` is false (observability/receipt.json lines 303-311). It adds alert routing, not telemetry retention or recoverable state.

alternatives.name: ntfy
alternatives.why_not_default: ntfy is the local inbox at the end of the alert route. The route was proven (observability/receipt.json lines 303-311), and `ntfy_message` persisted through a restart on synthetic data (observability/backends/receipt.json line 92). Delivery to a phone, email or other external destination was not tested (`external_delivery_tested` false). It is a notification layer, not telemetry or state retention.

alternatives.name: opentelemetry-collector
alternatives.why_not_default: This is the core runtime inside the contrib distribution (c14). The receipt lists only the `otelcol-contrib_0.161.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz` asset (observability/receipt.json), and the standalone core binary was never run on its own. It is proven only as part of c14, so it is not an independent winner.

alternatives.name: Restic
alternatives.why_not_default: Restic is the only candidate with native backup and restore evidence. blueprints/us-equities/hosting/backup/receipt.json records init, backup, `check --read-data` and `restore --verify` all exiting 0. It restored 22 files (160642 bytes), with 22 sha256sum OK lines and an independent byte match. The selection, however, was only static public reference files (selected-files.txt, source.sha256), with `live_databases` 0. No Loki, Prometheus, SQLite or broker-journal data was backed up. The repository, password and restore were all on one host (`off_host_destination` false). No backup timer is enabled, retention ran only as a dry run with 0 deletions, and key escrow is `not_configured`. It meets the recovery need only if extended to live telemetry state and off-host storage. It backs up the telemetry stack rather than replacing any part of it.

alternatives.name: sandbox-runtime
alternatives.why_not_default: sandbox-runtime is the only candidate with evidence bearing on the requirement clause 'without granting research workers broker execution authority' (packet line 498). The evidence shows filesystem restriction only (evidence/receipts/runtime-tools.json): allowed write exit 0, denied read exit 1, separate denied write exit 1, and no host file created. Network denial was configured but not exercised, and an overlapping read/write exclusion produced exit 0 into an ephemeral hidden mount. Nothing tests broker credentials or network isolation, and it is not a VM boundary. It is a restriction layer to pair with the telemetry winners, not a telemetry or retention layer.

alternatives.name: opensandbox
alternatives.why_not_default: The only evidence is an upstream README (source review); nothing was run locally. The pin is server/v0.2.3, while the packet lists the latest upstream release as release-1.1.0 with `pin_behind_upstream` true (packet lines 19 and 27). This is untested, not failed.

alternatives.name: modal
alternatives.why_not_default: The only evidence is the PyPI page (source review). `modal run` runs paid cloud code, and it was not executed. It is managed hosting, outside the local no-paid-hosting scope (packet limitations, line 496). This is untested, not failed.

alternatives.name: e2b
alternatives.why_not_default: The only evidence is an upstream README; an import alone is not an end-to-end sandbox test. The self-hosting guide targets AWS/GCP infrastructure. There is no local execution evidence. This is untested, not failed.

alternatives.name: mlflow
alternatives.why_not_default: The only evidence is an upstream README. No tracking server was run and no experiment was recorded. It covers experiment lineage rather than operational telemetry retention. This is untested, not failed.

alternatives.name: phoenix
alternatives.why_not_default: The only evidence is an upstream README. The server was never launched and no app was instrumented. The license is ELv2 with restrictions (upstream metadata reports NOASSERTION). Traces are disabled in the adopted Collector and no trace database was deployed, so its trace role is not demonstrated. This is untested, not failed.

limits: The external URL evidence for c1, c4, c7, c9 and c11 (upstream READMEs and PyPI) was not fetched. Their source-review status comes from the packet cards and was not verified by this lane.
Not opened: observability/followup-receipt.json, observability/restart-receipt.json, and the recipe and README files. The post-refinement Loki restart scope is therefore unverified.
fixtures/observability-check.json was not opened in this round. Its expected answer (sum 42, service_count 4) and sha256 are copied from observability/receipt.json lines 236-244.
Only the headers of tests/test_observability.py and tests/test_observability_backends_alerts.py were read, not the full files. No tests or commands were run.
All results come from receipts recorded on 2026-09-19 and were not re-observed now.
The packet withholds the current choice, decision and rationale, so this verdict is not reconciled against them.
The requirement text is shared across the layer's group (packet line 499), so fit was judged against the layer title and its scope terms.

Revision round: all refuter findings were checked against the cited sources. Accepted and corrected: the failed attempts rest on documentation only (major); the persistence checks used synthetic data; 80770 was re-checked only after a Collector restart; the Restic overturn clause was inconsistent; the alerts test cannot compare stacks; the Dagu and c1 facts lacked inline citations.
Skill: <host-path>/SKILL.md (preloaded). No TypeSafe inference results were supplied and none were made. Every judgment here is this lane's own source review; no provider judgments are retained.
Model: the schema value is fixed at opus/high as instructed. The client reports the actual model as claude-opus-5-5[1m].
open_gaps: Retention of failed attempts through the telemetry stack is not observed. `retained_failed_attempts` (observability/receipt.json lines 370-375) is prose written by the receipt's authors. All native client runs exited 0 with correct answers, and no failed native run was shown being ingested or queried. The failed-status handling is covered only by the offline tests/test_observability.py helper test.

Restart persistence for Loki and Prometheus was shown on synthetic data (`synthetic_fixture` true, observability/backends/receipt.json line 87). It also predates the later Loki label and SDK dashboard refinements (line 117).

The 80770 SDK receipt total was re-checked after a Collector restart only. No receipt shows those records surviving a Loki restart. That later scope is delegated to observability/followup-receipt.json, which this lane did not open.

The SDK receipt lane summarized 2 earlier receipts rather than making new model calls (observability/receipt.json line 248). The SDK native turn histogram was not observed (`native_turn_histogram_observed` false), including in a bounded flush experiment.

There is no high availability: all six services run as single-host WSL user services, and 'Single-host persistence is not replication or an off-host backup' (observability/backends/receipt.json line 106).

Telemetry is not backed up off-host. Restic covered 22 static public files only (`live_databases` 0), with `off_host_destination` false and key escrow `not_configured`. Restic retention ran only as a dry run, and no backup timer is enabled.
Traces are disabled and no trace database was deployed. phoenix and mlflow were never run.
The retained spool has no automatic expiry. Loss and recovery under a full disk or an extended backend outage were not tested (observability/receipt.json line 258).
Retention settings are configured but were not aged out during the check.
Alert delivery to external destinations was not tested (`external_delivery_tested` false).

The evidence does not show research workers being kept away from broker execution authority. sandbox-runtime proved filesystem restriction only; network denial and broker-credential isolation were not tested (evidence/receipts/runtime-tools.json).

Supervision of owned processes is not established. Dagu returned 401 without authentication, which 'proves expected anonymous protection, not authenticated workflow functionality' (observability/receipt.json lines 284-286).
No measured comparison against another telemetry stack was run. The winners were chosen by native acceptance, not by comparison.

arms: baseline: otelcol-contrib 0.161.0 + Loki 3.7.8 + Prometheus 3.14.0 (c14, c6, c5)

recovery (evaluated separately; does not displace a baseline component): Restic 0.19.1 (c8) backing up the baseline's live Loki/Prometheus storage to an off-host repository and restoring onto a fresh host
challenger: any other adopted or catalogued telemetry/trace stack (e.g. phoenix c11 with traces enabled) run on the same fixture and metrics 1-5
overturn_protocol.metric:
Pass/fail per arm on each of these checks:
(1) The native-client fixture answer (sum 42, service_count 4), with collected usage matching native usage.
(2) The deduplicated SDK receipt total_tokens (baseline 80770) staying the same across a restart of both the collector and the storage backend.
(3) Historical metric and log retention after a backend restart, on real run telemetry rather than only synthetic data.
(4) Forbidden-marker absence on the privacy canary.
(5) A deliberately failed native run that is ingested and queryable with usage_status preserved.
(6) For the recovery arm only: a verified restore (check --read-data exit 0, independent byte match) that includes live Loki and Prometheus storage and an off-host copy, with the same queries answered afterward.

why_selected:
The requirement (packet line 498) asks the layer to keep scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state from native research runs. These three components are the collection and retention path that was actually run with native clients. This is a telemetry-retention verdict. It does not decide the recovery, backup or sandbox parts of the layer.

- **c14, OpenTelemetry Collector contrib 0.161.0.** observability/receipt.json records `otelcol-contrib validate` exiting 0 and a verified upstream archive checksum. In native_client_acceptance (lines 163-202), native Codex 0.155.1 and Claude 2.1.278 each ran the fixtures/observability-check.json task, exited 0 and returned the correct answer. For Codex, `collected_turn_histogram_matches_native_usage` is true (line 182). For Claude, `collected_request_logs_and_metrics_match` is true (line 201).
- **c6, Loki 3.7.8.** The native Loki query deduplicated per `receipt_id` and returned `total_tokens` "80770" (lines 122-127). In sdk_receipt_lane, `after_collector_restart_total_tokens` is also 80770 (lines 251-252). That value was re-checked only after a Collector restart, not after a Loki restart. The input was 2 metadata summaries of earlier SDK receipts, not new model calls (line 248). Unknown usage is kept, not set to zero (line 254).
- **c5, Prometheus 3.14.0.** `promtool` checks exited 0, and all seven scrape targets returned "1" (lines 271-279). The historical privacy-canary query returned ["7","7"] (lines 130-137). That canary is an independent synthetic review, not an inference task (line 314).

**Restart persistence was proven on synthetic data.** observability/backends/receipt.json lines 85-98 show `loki_log` and `prometheus_historical_sample` persisting through one restart of the backends, with `synthetic_fixture` true. Those checks predate the later Loki label and SDK dashboard refinements (line 117). The binaries ran natively; the retained data in the restart check was synthetic.

**Failed attempts are only partly supported.** `retained_failed_attempts` (receipt lines 370-375) is prose written by the receipt's authors. Every native client run in the evidence succeeded, and no receipt shows the Collector, Loki or Prometheus ingesting and returning a failed native run. The only failed-status evidence is an offline unit test, which checks that the worker helper keeps `status` failed and `usage` None (tests/test_observability.py lines 32-40). The stack retaining failed attempts was not observed.

All results were recorded on 2026-09-19 as native command-line execution on one WSL host. None of this shows high availability or off-host storage, and no measured comparison against another telemetry stack was run.
